why: The output is a "blocked" answer, not an issue, so it has no expect lines and no proof entries. Nothing in it relies on a release, a deploy, a published page or anything else that exists only after merge, so the criterion holds by default. Blocking also fits the request. Issue #11 only asks a question ("why does mathlib use CommonJS and not ES modules?") and asks for no repository change, so there would be nothing to check at the pull request's head anyway. The reason given ("nothing for a builder to build or a verifier to check") is consistent with that.
